content.content:
Apply by reading the dependent and the prerequisite; there is nothing to run.
1. License: no element of the dependent contradicts the prerequisite. Fail on any contradicting element — name the element.
2. License: no element of the dependent adds a rule the prerequisite does not state. Fail on any such element — name it — including an element that restates a rule the prerequisite records as belonging to another recorded decision or as outside its own scope.
3. Applicability: the criterion is applied to the requirement sentence the dependent is meant to carry. Fail when the dependent carries no such sentence — empty or placeholder content — an absent elaboration is not a silent pass.
content.rationale: The dependent is a requirement sentence and the prerequisite is prose, so this edge is the natural-to-structured cell: the check is the licence clause, applied by reading, not running. The requirement's clauses are the end of an open draft read at the lifecycle, at the operation vocabulary and at the history, and C-DISCARD is where those readings are recorded. The licence has two limbs and the criterion states both: an elaboration may narrow what the prerequisite commits, but it may neither contradict the prerequisite nor add a rule the prerequisite does not state — including restating a rule the prerequisite records as another recorded decision's to state or as outside its own scope, which is out of licence even though it contradicts nothing. The criterion is applied to the requirement sentence the dependent is meant to carry, so a dependent that carries none (empty or placeholder) fails rather than passing vacuously; an absent elaboration proves nothing. Findings name the offending element; nothing is named in advance, so rewording the requirement or the prerequisite leaves the criterion intact.
